title: SpendReservation
description:
A hold placed on the rolling hourly budget before any signer is invoked (SPEC §5.3, SEC-002).

Lifecycle: created atomically in state `reserved` before signing; moves to `committed` only after a paid response is confirmed; moves to `released` on terminal failure with no payment evidence; moves to `expired` once `expiresAtEpochMs` passes without resolution.

An expired reservation MUST NOT count toward the hourly budget. An ambiguous outcome (5xx, timeout, or network failure after the signature was transmitted) deliberately leaves the reservation in `reserved` until its TTL elapses rather than releasing it — releasing early would let a possibly-settled payment be double-spent against the cap (SPEC §6.7).

policyScope.description: Identifies the budget the reservation draws against. A single client instance uses one scope; a shared SpendStore across processes partitions by it (ADR-007).

requestFingerprint.description: SEC-009: binds method, normalized URL, body digest, and challenge hash. Contains no secrets — not headers, not cookies, not bearer tokens. Golden vectors freeze the construction so TypeScript and Python produce identical digests.

expiresAtEpochMs.description: createdAtEpochMs + 120000. The TTL is fixed at 120 seconds by SPEC §5.3 and is not configurable.
